entities.summary: Achiulf (b. 270 CE) was a prominent economist and social scientist of the Classical era, active in the Roman Empire. His work focused on the intersection of politics and economy, particularly in the context of monarchs and rulers. Achiulf's research influenced the development of political theory and governance in the ancient world. He is best known for his treatise on the economic and social implications of imperial expansion, which remains a foundational text in the field of political economy. The impact of Achiulf's work can be seen in the writings of later historians and thinkers, who built upon his ideas to shape our understanding of the ancient world. In a striking example of the enduring power of his ideas, Achiulf's treatise was rediscovered and reinterpreted by modern scholars in the 20th century, who saw it as a precursor to contemporary debates on globalization and economic inequality.
